clue.text: Talk about second copper infiltrating Norfolk town

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so these letters go into the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone discusses a second policeman going undercover in a small Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal, giving its symbol CU. DISS is a small market town in Norfolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk about a subject is a plain synonym for debating it at length.

clue.text: Fancy gentleman wearing flower

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the river surrounds the title

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: here the Dee
Sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A dapper gentleman with a flower in his buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword river, something that flows; the Dee runs through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to want it, so the noun is a craving or wish.

clue.text: Wild herb covering third of valley

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the herb goes around the picked letter

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

indicators.note: a third of the six-letter word valley is its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A wild herb spreads across a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and wild both describe untamed, fierce animals or people, a synonym.

clue.text: Below a den, hunter shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter is shot down near a den.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean beneath or lower down, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Wash unusually large item of clothing

indicators.note: unusually means arranged out of the normal order

parts.note: L is the size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: wash this oversized garment in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap worn around the shoulders is one example of a garment.

clue.text: Garment missing last pocket

indicators.note: missing its last means the final letter of the garment word is dropped

parts.note: trousers are a garment for the legs

explanation.surface: A garment lacking its final pocket, as if a tailor forgot one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' reads as a noun on the garment but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket something is to take it for oneself, a sense the verb shares with slipping cash into one's pocket.

clue.text: Ship aims to leave international harbour

indicators.note: to leave means to be taken out of the aiming word

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A ship intends to sail out of an international port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a vessel but is a verb: to send goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to carry or convey them, so it is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Some more volunteers picked up six balls

indicators.note: in a down answer picked up means lifted, read from bottom to top
some means a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cricket coach asks for more volunteers to field six balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled by one player from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, six consecutive deliveries by one bowler make up this unit of play.

clue.text: Growing rat eating very much

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the informer's word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to rat is to inform, or sing, to the police
well means very much, as in well pleased

explanation.surface: A rat is growing as it eats a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swelling is getting bigger, a synonym for expanding.

clue.text: Person's worried prior to European reaction

indicators.note: prior to means this scrambled piece comes before the abbreviation
worried means troubled or shaken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A person is anxious before a European's reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply or reaction to something, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Kept trimmed? Not husband

indicators.note: not the husband means his letter is taken out of the word for trimmed

parts.note: a beard trimmed off is shaved

explanation.surface: A wife wonders whether he kept his beard trimmed, or perhaps this isn't her husband at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Money kept aside rather than spent has been put by, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Knowledge of mostly easy answer condemned

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
mostly means the word is used without its final letter

explanation.surface: Knowing an easy answer and having it condemned, as in a quiz judged harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims EASY to EAS; 'condemned' rearranges EAS with ANSWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is being conscious or informed of something, close to knowledge in meaning.

clue.text: Observe the French ship at all events

parts.note: to regard something is to look at or observe it
le is French for the
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at the French ship no matter what.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean anyway, whatever happens: an idiom pairing.

clue.text: Too advanced group of musicians

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A complaint that a band of musicians is too advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition or as well, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Current chap consuming alcohol before church — that's of concern

indicators.note: before puts the pieces ahead of the church abbreviation

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the chap holds the drink

parts.note: a chap is a man
port is a fortified wine
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A modern man drinking before going to church is a worrying matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Of concern and of moment both mean significant, so concern matches in the sense of weight or significance.

clue.text: Devon temples demolished making housing estates?

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down, so the letters of these words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Temples in Devon are knocked down to make room for new housing estates.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a housing estate is one kind of building project.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing estates are new building projects on cleared land, one example of property schemes.

clue.text: Wide, costly piano exchanged for tuba, initially

indicators.note: exchanged for means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: costly means expensive
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word tuba

explanation.surface: An expensive piano is traded in for a tuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' and 'tuba' suggest instruments; one is the abbreviation P, the other gives its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive and wide both mean broad in range or area, a synonym.

clue.text: Stress about one day's mishap

indicators.note: about means around, so the stress word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: stress on a syllable is its accent
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: The stress of a single day's mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky event, a synonym for an unplanned mischance.

clue.text: Ten Verdi works turned up

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Ten works by the composer Verdi have turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like operas by Verdi but signals rearranging; 'turned up' looks like appeared but means upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned up is flipped over, upside down, a synonym in that physical sense.

clue.text: Walk disregarding a learner's state of health

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so these letters are removed from the walk word

parts.note: a constitutional is a walk taken for one's health
L is the abbreviation for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A healthy walk that ignores a novice's physical condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's constitution is their physical make-up and general health.

clue.text: Avoids girls

definitions.meaning: fails to hit or deliberately skips, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is fails to meet or dodges; the plural noun is the title for young unmarried women.

clue.text: Finished chapter and left, thus upsetting editor

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting means turning over, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A writer finished the chapter and left, upsetting the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shut-down business is finished, ended for good: a synonym.

clue.text: Detective Inspector goes over each thought

indicators.note: going over means turning back on itself, so the letters of the rank abbreviation are read backwards

parts.note: DI is the police abbreviation for Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police detective reviews every thought in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought and a notion are the same thing: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Manufacturing trouble east of river

indicators.note: in an across answer east of means to the right, so this piece comes after the river

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan
a trial is a nuisance or trouble

explanation.surface: Factory trouble breaks out east of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial describes factories and the making of goods, so it matches as an adjective.

clue.text: Upper-class rogue I'd regularly prodded

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A posh villain admits he was pushed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone into action is to encourage or press them, a synonym.

clue.text: Practically monstrous old writer

indicators.note: practically means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: monstrous means huge

explanation.surface: An old author who was almost a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Hugo was the French author of Les Misérables.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist Victor Hugo is an example of an author.

clue.text: Raving loony in Ghent hugging American

indicators.note: hugging means holding inside, so the abbreviation sits within the scrambled letters
loony means crazy, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wild person in Ghent hugs an American visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' rearranges IN GHENT to ENTHING; 'hugging' puts US inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Raving about something is gushing over it enthusiastically, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Filipinos essentially packing trunks

indicators.note: packing means containing, so the answer is carried within these words

explanation.surface: Filipinos are said to be packing trunks for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunks' suggests luggage, but means elephants' snouts.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's trunk is its long snout, so trunks are a kind of nose.

clue.text: Pond-dweller bit European

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: A pond creature that's a bit European.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog larva living in ponds, an example of a pond creature.

clue.text: Doctor, turning sweet, almost put bandage on

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for doctor, as in the degree letters DD

indicators.note: turning means the trimmed sweet is read backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sweet is a dessert, a pudding course

explanation.surface: A doctor turns sweet and almost finishes dressing a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DESSERT to DESSER; 'turning' reverses it to RESSED. Sweet is British for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to clean and cover it with a bandage, the medical sense.
